disposition: partial: target L3, level_met none (tenancy), measured 2026-10-01 against CMake 4.4.3 (tier A: the File API codemodel-v2 for cross-file dependencies and CMake's own command trace for references, calibration/oracles/cmake-file-api) and universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B, L1) on fmtlib/fmt 12.2.0, nlohmann/json v3.12.0 and bulletphysics/bullet3 3.25, the one larger multi-directory project (58 CMake files; configured with CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 because it declares cmake_minimum_required below 3.5). L1 excellent: sym_recall and sym_precision .9952 over 208 definitions (207 matched); the one miss is fmt's `fmt::fmt-c`, an ALIAS target ctags does not list (a target CMake lets a link name), and the one oracle-only target (fmt's non-error-test) is written inside a string passed to file(WRITE), which no static reader of the file sees; the three bullet3 *.pc.cmake pkg-config templates parse with errors and extract nothing (files_with_error 3). L2 excellent: ref_recall and ref_precision 1 over 62 pairs (a literal argument of an executed target_link_libraries or add_dependencies whose target the same file defines; arguments spelled with a variable or a generator expression, 4 of 26 link commands, are left out of the truth). The incumbent cmakeextract.go reads the same subjects at sym_precision .9200 and ref_precision .8986 (lang-parity: every L1 metric of the dialect is at least the incumbent's; REFUSED only because the target is not met). L3 unmet: xref_precision 1 (2 of 2 edges) but xref_recall .037 (2 of 54 oracle cross-file dependencies). Cause 1, the strategy: a CMake target name is global, an import graph is not. add_subdirectory(dir) and include() are imports, so a name resolves only from the importing file to the imported one (a parent to its child), and 52 of the 54 dependencies run the other way: a child directory linking its ancestor's target (nlohmann/json 5, fmt 1) or one directory linking a sibling's (bulletphysics/bullet3 46: examples to src libraries). Only fmt's 2 parent-to-child edges are import-bound and found. Resolving them needs a build-namespace strategy (a name resolves to the file that defines it anywhere in the repository, or in an ancestor or sibling directory), an Opus row (LB-F128, O375). Cause 2, tenancy: throughput .71 MB per CPU-second against the 1.0 floor (the harness reads level_met none whatever the metrics grade, tenancy being always required): uyha/tree-sitter-cmake v0.7.5 parses at about 1.1 to 1.2 MB per CPU-second in the wasm engine with an empty query, the eight definition patterns bring that to .9 to 1.0, and the link attachment (five sibling patterns) to .7 (O377, LB-F129). The attachment reaches a link command at most four commands after its target in the same block (57 of 61 such targets across the subjects within two, none beyond four); a link written elsewhere in the file, in another directory's file or inside an if() the target is not a child of attaches to nothing. Not dispatched: internal/fusion/register.go keeps CMakeLists.txt and .cmake on cmakeextract.go; the integrator re-runs lang-parity after item calls' D1 change.
